cards.b: Gene: a length of DNA that codes for a protein. Allele: an alternative form of a gene.

cards.f: How is sex inherited in humans?
cards.b: Females XX, males XY. Every egg carries X; sperm carry X or Y, so there is a 50% (1 : 1) chance of a boy or girl.
Haploid: one set of chromosomes (23 in human gametes). Diploid: two sets, 23 pairs in human body cells.
Nuclear division giving genetically identical cells. Used for growth, repair, replacement of cells and asexual reproduction.
Reduction division: chromosome number halved from diploid to haploid, giving genetically different cells. Produces gametes.
Genotype: the alleles present (e.g. Tt). Phenotype: the observable features (e.g. tall).
Homozygous: two identical alleles (TT or tt), pure-breeding. Heterozygous: two different alleles (Tt), not pure-breeding.
Dominant: expressed if present. Recessive: only expressed when no dominant allele is present.

cards.f: Ratio from Tt × Tt and from Tt × tt
cards.b: Tt × Tt: 3 dominant : 1 recessive phenotype (1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt). Tt × tt: 1 : 1.

cards.f: Pedigree clue: unaffected parents have an affected child
cards.b: The condition is caused by a recessive allele, and both parents must be heterozygous.
Continuous: range between extremes (body length), histogram. Discontinuous: limited categories (ABO blood groups), bar chart.
A genetic change; the way new alleles are formed.
Variation; many offspring; struggle for survival/competition; better-adapted survive and reproduce more; they pass on their alleles.
Humans select individuals with desirable features, cross them, select the best offspring, repeat over many generations.
A mutation gives resistance; the antibiotic kills non-resistant bacteria; resistant ones survive, reproduce and pass on the allele (e.g. MRSA).

short.q: Tall (T) is dominant to short (t). Two heterozygous plants are crossed. Give the genotypes and phenotypic ratio of the offspring. [3]
short.model: Gametes T or t from each parent give 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt, which is 3 tall : 1 short.
points: gametes T and t from each parent

short.q: Two unaffected parents have a child with a recessive condition. Explain how this is possible. [2]
short.model: Both parents are heterozygous carriers; each passes on the recessive allele to the child, who is homozygous recessive.
points: child inherits a recessive allele from each

short.q: Explain how a population of bacteria becomes resistant to an antibiotic. [4]
short.model: A mutation gives a few bacteria resistance; the antibiotic kills the others; the resistant bacteria survive and reproduce, passing on the allele so a resistant strain develops.

short.q: State two differences between mitosis and meiosis. [2]
short.model: Mitosis gives genetically identical cells and keeps the chromosome number; meiosis gives genetically different cells and halves the chromosome number.

short.q: Describe how selective breeding could be used to produce cows with a high milk yield. [3]
short.model: Select cows and bulls with high milk yield, breed them together, select the best offspring and repeat over many generations.
